fluff.overview:
The Patron is one of the oldest IndustrialMech designs still in service, first produced by Atrean Robotics around 2470 as a specialized ammunition loader for the Icarus-series BattleMechs of the Free Worlds League. At fifteen tons, the Patron was purpose-built to operate within 'Mech bays, small enough to navigate tight maintenance spaces yet capable of lifting several tons of munitions at once with its torso-mounted hoist. The design proved so successful that Atrean Robotics expanded to sixteen worlds across three League districts before the Succession Wars drove the company out of business.

For centuries, surviving Patrons continued to serve throughout Free Worlds League military formations, valued above all for their reliability and mechanical simplicity. Following the Jihad, Graham-Davis Enterprises on Tamarind resumed production and dramatically expanded the Patron's role, introducing armed variants that transformed this humble LoaderMech into a capable militia and security platform for planetary defense forces across the Inner Sphere.
fluff.capabilities:
The base Patron LoaderMech is specifically designed for use in BattleMech bays and military support facilities. At fifteen tons, the design is small enough to pose no danger to most equipment and too small to do any real harm to a BattleMech, making it an ideal logistics platform for operating in close proximity to billion-C-bill war machines. The centerpiece of the design is a standard lift hoist mounted in the right torso, capable of moving seven tons of materials at once, more than sufficient for loading ammunition, swapping damaged components, or repositioning heavy equipment within a repair bay.

A sprayer system provides coolant distribution capability, allowing the Patron to service overheated BattleMechs returning from combat. The Vlar 30 PowerStack fuel cell engine provides a modest cruising speed of twenty-one kilometers per hour, entirely adequate for a machine that rarely ventures beyond the confines of a military installation. The Type 7 IndiPlate commercial-grade armor offers only token protection, a deliberate concession to the Patron's non-combat role and weight constraints. The design lacks any weapons systems or sophisticated targeting equipment, relying on a basic Apple Communicator system for coordination with bay crews and supporting technicians.
fluff.history:
The Patron's history stretches back to the Age of War, making it one of the longest-serving IndustrialMech designs in the Inner Sphere. First produced around 2470 by Atrean Robotics on Atreus, the original PTN-1 was designed exclusively to reload the Icarus-series BattleMechs then entering service with the Free Worlds League Military. The Patron's success in this logistics role transformed Atrean Robotics from a small manufacturer into a company spanning sixteen worlds across three Free Worlds League districts.

As BattleMech designs proliferated beyond the Icarus series, Atrean Robotics responded with a more versatile generic LoaderMech configuration around 2550, phasing out the specialized PTN-1. This updated Patron served throughout the League's BattleMech formations for centuries, becoming a ubiquitous presence in 'Mech bays across Free Worlds space. The devastation of the Succession Wars ultimately destroyed Atrean Robotics, but surviving Patrons continued to serve for generations, evidence of the design's durability and simplicity.

The Patron's story took an unexpected turn during the Jihad, when Graham-Davis Enterprises on Tamarind resumed production of the LoaderMech following the Paul Coup that fractured the Free Worlds League. New-build Patrons supported forces loyal to Photon Brett-Marik as they battled both Word of Blake invaders and Lyran opportunists. The demand for any available military assets during this desperate period inspired GDE to develop the PTN-2 MilitiaMech in 3076, arming the venerable Patron with light machine guns and rocket launchers for militia defense.

The armed Patron's combat debut in the Duchy of Tamarind exceeded all expectations. Local infantry defenders equipped with the new PTN-2 scattered bandit raiders who had anticipated facing only unarmed support 'Mechs, and the resulting publicity drove demand for an improved model. Graham-Davis introduced the PTN-2M PatrolMech by 3083, upgrading the armor to military-grade plating and adding proper fire control and targeting systems. The PTN-2M found a growing market throughout the former Free Worlds League and the Duchy of Tamarind-Abbey, as well as among mercenary companies and private security firms, establishing the Patron as an unlikely but effective light security platform alongside its centuries-old role as a logistics workhorse.
fluff.deployment: The PTN-2M represents the refined evolution of the armed Patron concept, redesigned as a dedicated PatrolMech for the post-Jihad security market. Graham-Davis Enterprises upgraded the armor from vulnerable commercial-grade plating to standard Maximillian 60 military armor, a critical improvement that addressed the PTN-2's most glaring weakness. The weapons loadout was streamlined to four LFN Linblad light machine guns and three Death Blossom rocket launcher tens, with the addition of a Neil 2000 communications system and TRSS Eagle Eye targeting system providing greatly improved fire control and situational awareness. GDE positioned the PTN-2M against the Coventry Metal Works Copper SecurityMech, billing it as offering greater reach at a lower price, though at half the Copper's ground speed and with less armor protection. The Patron can be found throughout the Inner Sphere, primarily in the former Free Worlds League, with newer versions sold within the Duchy of Tamarind and to its allies. Graham-Davis also markets the design to mercenary and private security companies with background checks to limit misuse. SecurityMechs of this type often perform double duty, helping load trucks when threat levels are low and guarding facilities at night.
